page: Microsoft Azure E128-64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is configured with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, providing 7559 GB of capacity, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multiple workloads. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core (2891.0) and multi-core (26776.0) tests, as well as Passmark CPU scores (94640.85). Memory performance is strong, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 206.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 133.04 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in software compilation, image processing, and single-threaded gzip compression.

In database and data-handling scenarios, the server performs in the top tier, registering 37846.03 on Passmark database operations and a strong 101.98 million operations per second on Redis SET operations. Although it lacks a dedicated GPU, the high-frequency CPU cores and memory capacity support top-tier LLM inference speeds for small models, processing 5186.0 tokens per second for prompts and 399.01 tokens per second for text generation.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and large local storage capacity offer high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, reducing the need for multi-node clustering. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training or large-scale LLM inference. This configuration is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
